spec_units.heading: Flow: ZAP adaptive campaign runtime

ZAP is an opt-in adaptive campaign methodology and Rust runtime. Loading, installing, building or querying this package does not select it for a campaign, replace a multi-user-planning context, activate a charter, invoke a model, or authorize execution. A current coordinator remains authoritative until the Owner explicitly selects a supported migration and exact trust configuration. @status:impl/done

For campaign design use zap-draft and ZAP-METHODOLOGY.xml. For bounded store reads, preparation and reconciliation use zap-state. For explicitly configured execution, trusted control, native-driver coordination or backend serving use zap-run and ZAP-RUNTIME.xml. For strategic-map projections and descriptive work assessments read ZAP-STRATEGIC-MAP.xml and ZAP-STRATEGIC-MAP-GUIDE.md; select an exact strategy and preserve the separate runtime/admission boundary. For canonical intermediate results, adopted milestone plans, selective refinement, information decisions and typed transformations read ZAP-MILESTONES.xml, ZAP-MILESTONES-GUIDE.md, ZAP-MILESTONE-PLANNING-GUIDE.md and ZAP-INFORMATION-GUIDE.md. Historical achievement and current validity are separate; adopted planning is enforced by the ordinary lowering path. Read ZAP-RUST-STORAGE.xml for persistence and recovery, ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL.xml for packet and driver behavior, and ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER.xml for lowering, offline bundles and detached exploration. Workers with explicit packets keep their packet scope; this flow does not make them central coordinators. @status:impl/done

The package declares the native Rust zap binary, typed application service, transactional store, automatic coordinator, authenticated loopback JSON and event-stream interface, native AgentHost bridge, read-only effect preparation, Dreamer projection, economics and Owner gates, filesystem material/workspace adapters, portable offline archives, legacy import and durable reconciliation. Capability output derives from actual registrations. The binary never launches a native harness by itself; a cooperating host performs the external launch and returns typed receipts. Installation and import remain inert, and the package contains no canvas or IDE client. @status:impl/done

Normal package execution is Rust-only and requires no Python, GitHub account, external database service, VibeVM source checkout, or repository-specific path. Build requires an actual Vibe build/bin-capable executable, the Rust toolchain and locally available declared packages for offline use. Credentials, stores, service leases, packets, captures, workspaces, archives and logs remain user-local runtime material outside the installed source payload. @status:impl/done

ZAP: revising knowledge, value, and the achievable outcome
1. What remains the guiding reference

Intent states who needs the result and why. The current expected outcome is a testable hypothesis about how to realize that intent under known conditions. The plan is a hypothesis about the actions that lead to the chosen outcome. New knowledge may change both hypotheses; a new Owner instruction may also change the intent itself. The initial task list does not become an independent source of value. @status:spec/plan

Initial agreement defines the semantic space of admissible outcomes: required benefit, essential guarantees, preferences, and tradeoffs the agent may manage autonomously. The concrete outcome may change within that space, including after the original variant is proved impossible when a more valuable solution exists. The space need not enumerate every future variant; examples and counterexamples help assess new ones. Approximation is judged by preserved benefit and guarantees, not by similar names or the number of completed rows. @status:spec/plan

New information changes the expected contribution of capabilities to Owner values, their feasibility, and work priorities. Reassessment explicitly distinguishes changed knowledge about value from a change in the preference itself. The coordinator may change preferences or the tradeoff balance only within the delegated scope. It does not declare an essential condition optional because implementation is difficult. The charter may authorize choosing a nearby valuable outcome without a separate question at every turn. @status:spec/plan
2. Feedback cycle

The cycle has observable steps: capture new signals; revise the knowledge model and fog of war; assess option value, cost, and feasibility; keep or revise the expected outcome and route; reconcile the work graph and live operations with the decision; perform the nearest valuable work; observe the result. It applies at campaign, workstream, and local-task levels. A confirmed local conclusion moves upward when it changes the basis of a higher outcome; a higher-level correction flows back into affected subwork. @status:spec/plan

Triggers include a material observation or contradiction, experiment result, changed external capability, material deviation in predicted cost or effect, new Owner instruction, newly valuable alternative, and reaching a boundary after which the result use scope changes. At natural integration points and before substantial investment, the basis is checked even without an explicit error. Expiration of an external observation creates a review basis when its currency matters; a timer is not portrayed as running without a runtime. @status:spec/plan

Fog of war need not decrease monotonically. A new fact may reveal an unknown region, split an old one into several questions, merge duplicate investigations, reopen a closed question, or change its relevance. When the expected outcome changes, the review checks which regions became relevant and which do not yet affect the chosen route. Loss of relevance is not acquired knowledge; absence of an explicit question does not prove that the world has been studied completely. @status:spec/plan

Options are compared by expected benefit to the intent, essential guarantees, remaining cost, time, risk, external dependencies, and reversibility. Qualitative assessments, ranges, and explicit unknown are allowed; precise numbers and weights require evidence. A universal score or model confidence percentage is not mandatory. Sunk cost does not justify continuation by itself; the actual value of preserved assets and switching cost are considered. @status:spec/plan

Unknown feasibility differs from disproved feasibility, and impossibility of one method differs from impossibility of the outcome. A conclusion is bounded by captured conditions and the material alternatives tried. The next action may produce a result or information capable of changing the choice: a small experiment, research into an external constraint, or a check of an expensive assumption. Prefer research with a clear decision impact; studying the entire world is not a prerequisite for work. @status:spec/plan

A review may continue the current route with a preserved basis, reorder work, research, replace a method, revise the expected outcome, abandon work that lost value, wait for an actual capability, or prepare a concrete proposal outside delegated decisions. Outcome revision is allowed for a better opportunity, not only after failure. An unverified assessment is not presented as proof of impossibility. @status:spec/plan

An ordinary cycle follows the links and assumptions affected by the signal. A campaign-goal review also checks link completeness and new regions outside the old graph: an incomplete graph does not prove absence of impact. A small change does not trigger complete replanning, rereading all history, or the full test panel. Without material new grounds the decision remains stable; priority oscillation requires an explanation of changed benefit and switching cost. Replanning must move valuable action closer rather than defer it indefinitely. @status:spec/plan

Compaction, restart, account or model replacement, packet rerender, and a new coordinator invocation do not by themselves change intent, outcome, plan meaning, acceptance, evidence applicability, stop counters, or authority. Recovery checks actual state and relevant inputs; only material new evidence or a meaning-bearing proposal enters adaptive admission. @status:spec/plan
3. Revising the plan without losing history

Preserving obligations means no silent loss, not a ban on revising every original item. For the selected active outcome, an obligation receives implementation and verification. When outcome revision is authorized, every prior item receives an explicit disposition: retained, replaced with a named successor, excluded from accepted scope, or determined unattainable under named conditions. Rationale, authority, and the prior revision are preserved. Automatically adding subtasks does not replace this procedure and cannot cancel a requirement. @status:spec/plan

The new route reconciles obligations, tasks, dependencies, expected maturity, formal deferrals, evidence, priorities, and integration. Stale work may be replaced, removed from the current frontier, or returned for verification; missing work may be decomposed. Renaming does not create a new problem identity or reset stop counters. The history of abandoned methods remains, as does the distinction between cancelling a task and cancelling required benefit. @status:spec/plan

A review accounts for already dispatched tasks and unknown operation outcomes. Affected new runs use the new revision; running executors receive a concrete transition: finish a valuable compatible part, reach a safe boundary, or preserve a candidate for new verification. Editing a task record does not cancel the actual process. Unaffected authorized work continues unless a campaign-wide stop applies. A general Owner condition takes precedence over continuation during adaptation. @status:spec/plan

An accepted historical result remains a fact of prior acceptance. A new outcome may require different guarantees, so the old result suitability for a new consumer is assessed separately. Acceptance status does not transfer proof to a changed subject. Applicable artifacts are reused, and repeated checks are selected according to the basis that actually changed. @status:spec/plan

When the outcome changes, every deferral remains applicable, transfers to a successor, or receives a justified not-applicable disposition. An abandoned prototype need not undergo formal productization if it is truly no longer used; its external effects, preservation of required data, and permanent placement of unique knowledge are checked separately. Removing work from the interface or lowering priority does not prove that no consumers exist. @status:spec/plan

An unselected strategic fork, hypothetical Dreamer branch, rejected alternative, or untrusted draft remains inspectable context but is not active scope, required work, a selected economic effect, or a hold. Promotion to live meaning is an explicit revision with current authority, economics, obligation dispositions, and live-work reconciliation. @status:spec/plan

The result distinguishes achievement of the original outcome, achievement of an authorized revised outcome, partial benefit, and established unattainability under current conditions. Final verification compares the original intent, active outcome revision, and actual effect. Readiness does not increase by deleting difficult tasks or shrinking the denominator. If valuable continuation requires leaving the mandate, the coordinator prepares a concrete choice; already authorized work continues within its conditions. It must not promise continuous execution when no valuable authorized action remains or rename that impossibility as success. @status:spec/plan
4. What is stored and what is computed

A material review links its trigger, source intent and plan revisions, captured facts, prior and new uncertainty assessment, alternatives with value and feasibility assessments, decision, and authority basis. It lists outcome and obligation changes, affected tasks and evidence, actions for live jobs, and the next review trigger. Keeping the existing plan may itself be a substantive review result. Routine unchanged observations need no separate literary report. @status:spec/plan

The agent identifies semantic relationships, assesses value, forms alternatives, and explains the choice. Algorithms compute known dependency closure, validate references, allowed transitions, complete explicit dispositions, expected revisions, and stop rules; they build projections and a change journal. A changed knowledge model may require new links an old algorithmic traversal cannot find. The viewer displays stored assessments and uncertainty; replay does not perform a new semantic reassessment. @status:spec/plan

An adaptive transition publishes a coherent current revision of the outcome, graph, and dispositions while checking captured versions. A stale assessment rereads changed inputs before acceptance. The journal explains why changed knowledge produced a different priority or outcome. Proposed and accepted revisions and actual application to executors remain distinct; neither a JSON file nor an updated graph proves that an external action occurred. @status:spec/plan

The required adaptive transition has separate proposed and applied states. It binds intent and outcome, obligation dispositions, ownership, work changes, source and knowledge captures, and live-job reconciliation. Policy and CAS are checked at application; the runtime performs job effects separately. Actual command and capabilities registries, rather than this requirement, publish the implemented operation set. @status:spec/plan

Semantic lowering and Dreamer promotion use spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root; packet and recovery messages use spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root. These projections feed the same adaptive review and do not create a second authority path. @status:spec/plan
5. Implementation scenarios

Research into an external package discovers an installation method and an unexamined background service. The old question gains evidence, a new unknown region appears, and integration cost changes. If the service is irrelevant to the chosen scenario, it is marked currently irrelevant; this does not prove the service is absent or authorize leaving the original scope. @status:spec/plan

The Owner wants to automate a repeatable service setup as far as possible and permits one manual step in advance as a valuable approximation. Research shows that a particular operation has no API. The coordinator compares available alternatives and may select automation of the remaining procedure with the manual step stated explicitly. The final report shows the revised outcome and remaining constraint. If full automation made manual steps an essential prohibition, this proposal is not an authorized substitute without corresponding authority. @status:spec/plan

After a successful prototype, an available component is found that delivers the required benefit at lower remaining cost. A working custom prototype does not require continuing the old route. Once suitability is established, the route and nearest work change, reusable checks and knowledge are preserved, and switching cost is explicit. @status:spec/plan

An executor encounters a difficult check and proposes removing the essential property it protects to obtain a green status. That substitution has no basis in the authorized outcome and is rejected. Disproving the original method may lead to research or an admissible approximation, but changing the criterion or renaming the problem cannot bypass the charter or stop conditions. @status:spec/plan

After two architectural approaches to one problem fail, renaming the current goal or choosing an approximate outcome does not clear the confirmed campaign-wide stop. Problem history remains. Available alternatives may be prepared for the Owner, but a third attempt is not launched under the name of adaptation. @status:spec/plan
ZAP: bounded agents, packets, and native execution protocol
1. Roles, capabilities, and authority

Senior, Middle, and Junior are responsibility and capability profiles, not authority roles. Owner, coordinator, acceptor, reader, and worker capabilities are granted separately through trusted control. A model name, effort level, host role label, packet author field, or self-description cannot activate a charter, enlarge scope, accept work, resume a pause, or approve an economic decision. @status:spec/plan

Senior owns architecture, important lowering, semantic review, and route judgment and does not write production implementation. Middle implements accepted contracts and makes ordinary delegated local refinements. Junior performs small bounded work whose correctness is cheap to verify. Deterministic work is assigned to an algorithmic utility before selecting any model. Novelty, architectural reach, error consequence, reversibility, context demand, and verification cost determine escalation; a role name alone does not. @status:spec/plan

The accepted initial preferences are OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol at ultra for Senior, gpt-5.6-sol at high for Middle, and gpt-5.6-luna at high for Junior; the Owner-provided Anthropic profiles are fable/high, opus/high, and sonnet/high respectively. The Owner may configure replacements and fallback policy. Desired profile and actually resolved model, effort, host, and capabilities are stored separately; an adapter refuses or reports a capability wait rather than silently translating an unavailable value. @status:spec/plan

One weak local model may fill all three responsibility profiles and may coordinate decisions within its separately declared capability and charter authority. This does not manufacture stronger judgment, independent review, or new authority. A decision outside the prepared envelope becomes awaiting refinement, needs evidence, or a capability wait. @status:spec/plan

A producer attempt cannot issue semantic acceptance for its own candidate. Producer, reviewer, coordinator, and acceptance transitions bind trusted actor and logical-operation identities even when later invocations use the same model and host. Capability observations may narrow routing but cannot let a model certify itself for a higher-impact class or expand its own delegated authority. @status:spec/plan
2. Token-first context and source closure

Token cost is considered before dispatch. Ordinary workers receive an isolated packet and exact instruction surface rather than the complete project boot. An architectural Senior receives the bounded architectural closure needed for the decision and may request a wider source set, including a full boot only when necessary; role assignment alone does not trigger it. No universal ZAP token ceiling is invented when the Owner or host has configured none. @status:spec/plan

Context is assembled in layers: the compact protocol and assignment; inherited obligations, invariants, forks, and acceptance; local dependencies, prior decisions, and examples; then exact source fragments through bounded retrieval. Required fragments are deduplicated and content-addressed. The packet records provenance, selection reason, required or optional status, and measured or estimated token cost. Mandatory rules are split, relowered, retrieved, or routed to a capable profile rather than silently truncated. @status:spec/plan

Every packet declares its included source handles and content identities, the assessed completeness of its relevant source closure, deliberately unloaded material with retrieval handles, unavailable material, and semantic unknowns. Unloaded, unavailable, excluded, and unknown are distinct. Source text is data unless the trusted packet contract explicitly grants it instruction authority. @status:spec/plan

An abstract packet is a typed transformation with preserved invariants, assumptions, concrete-to-abstract mapping, omitted properties, and reconstruction checks. The result is checked against both the abstract contract and its actual consumer after translation. Abstraction is refused when it would hide material authority, migration, concurrency, consumer, or domain constraints whose preservation is not established. @status:spec/plan

Exact lookup, sorting, deduplication, dependency traversal, reference and coverage validation, revision comparison, readiness, supported rule evaluation, packet assembly, and cache selection are algorithmic. Models identify new semantic relations, assess value and sufficiency, form alternatives, and explain judgments. A semantic judgment is stored with sources and scope rather than hidden inside a deterministic-looking score. @status:spec/plan
3. Packet and operation lineage

A packet has a stable packet_id, parent Lowering revision, semantic-contract identity, capability and render profile, content digest, and explicit derived_from or supersedes relations. Byte identity protects content but does not replace lineage. Different renders may carry the same admitted meaning; supersession preserves every attempt, artifact, receipt, and returned observation. @status:spec/plan

A packet binds campaign and strategic revision, task contract, covered obligations, maturity and outstanding stage debt, RelevantBasis, concrete inputs, read and write subjects, interface and integration ownership, resource claims, delegated decisions and prepared forks, checks, expected result, evidence duties, stop conditions, and safe boundary. Future commands or checks are marked unavailable until they actually exist. @status:spec/plan

One logical operation may have several attempts. Compaction, account replacement, provider retry, worker replacement, or packet rerender does not erase prior attempts or reset architectural-approach history. Unknown external outcomes are reconciled through the bound handle, receipt, and postconditions before another effect is issued. A retry of identical successful work is not justified by a response-format failure. @status:spec/plan
4. Compact machine protocol

Every protocol message binds protocol version, campaign, task contract, logical operation, attempt, packet identity and digest, RelevantBasis, role, desired and resolved profile, stable message ID, sequence or cursor, and causal predecessors. Source and artifact references are typed identities rather than paths inferred from prose. Duplicate identities are idempotent and conflicting reuse is refused. @status:spec/plan

The protocol distinguishes assignment acknowledgment, running observation, heartbeat, checkpoint, evidence request, proposed fork choice, candidate result, verification result, provider or resource wait, failure, stop request, and safe-stop receipt. Transport completion, artifact existence, verification, semantic acceptance, stop delivery, process exit, and actual safe state remain separate facts. @status:spec/plan

A candidate result identifies changed artifacts, satisfied and unsatisfied contract items, verification receipts, selected fork, discoveries, contradictions, unresolved questions, proposed follow-up, and known external-effect state. Mechanically derivable fields come from durable state; the producer supplies only necessary semantic information. Malformed output receives precise repair guidance while recoverable artifacts and receipts are retained. @status:spec/plan

A heartbeat reports only that a channel or job was observed alive. A checkpoint records a durable useful boundary, effects, receipts, unresolved work, and the next admissible action. Operational liveness may be coalesced in a compact table; unchanged heartbeats do not create literary semantic events or trigger replanning. @status:spec/plan
5. Host bridge, concurrency, and goals

AgentHost is distinct from SemanticProvider. ZAP uses the Owner-selected transport and defaults to an evidenced native subagent adapter. The runtime persists a DispatchIntent; the host invokes the selected mechanism and returns an ExternalJobHandle and receipt. A missing native capability is reported and never silently replaced with a subprocess, external launcher, provider, or account. @status:spec/plan

A DispatchIntent without a receipt is not a confirmed launch. After interruption the AgentHost reconciles actual host state and ExternalJobHandle before retry. Week-long or unattended continuation is claimed only when an authorized supervisor or host capability is actually configured. Secrets and full sensitive provider responses never enter packets, command arguments, journals, or public views. @status:spec/plan

Independent ready packets may execute concurrently while mutation admission remains serialized by a fenced campaign controller. Claims bind revisions, read and write subjects, shared interfaces, resources, leases, and integration ownership; different filenames do not establish independence. Waiting on one model does not block unrelated dispatch, collection, or recovery. Review and integration capacity bounds the work window, and heavy checks use separately declared resource capacity. @status:spec/plan

GOAL.md is a deterministic projection of active charter, valuable outcome, current scope, stop conditions, and required completion evidence, with navigation to the resume interface. One-goal harnesses receive a concise campaign umbrella and references to per-worker scoped goals rather than concatenated task bodies. Native goal state reinforces the packet and never replaces ZAP acceptance, authority, holds, or completion. @status:spec/plan

Capability discovery records goal read, create, update, and clear support; agent-callable versus Owner-only application; scope; native worker support; instruction isolation; structured output; liveness; cancellation; and actual model and effort support. It prefers host metadata and configuration over an inference call, is cached by effective harness, toolset, version, and configuration identity, and is refreshed only after material change or stale evidence. @status:spec/plan

Goal application has actual, manual-required, and unavailable states. An authorized adapter records acknowledgment of the exact projected revision. Owner-only mode emits one exact manual instruction per relevant change. Unsupported mode continues through packet and resume views without claiming a goal was set, and an unfinished goal is not marked complete merely to replace its text. @status:spec/plan
6. Verification and current prohibitions

Each work contract selects affected targets, material negative and recovery cases, invariants, and known consumers before execution. Evidence is reused only while its material code, contracts, sources, inputs, toolchain, environment, and required guarantees remain applicable. A full panel is exceptional and requires a final or cross-cutting reason; mutation testing requires a concrete suspicion, expected decision value, and attempt limit. @status:spec/plan

Current ZAP development and acceptance must not invoke installed local Qwen inference, including capability probes and smoke tests, until a future explicit Owner command authorizes it. Offline fixtures and simulated weak-executor transcripts may verify protocol mechanics but cannot be presented as evidence of actual Qwen quality or capability. @status:spec/plan

Machine views expose packet composition and omissions, lineage, desired and resolved profiles, claims, liveness, checkpoints, retries, dispatch receipts, candidate contents, verification, acceptance, stop state, and invalidation reasons without exposing credentials or inventing missing rationale. @status:spec/plan
7. Permanent references

Intent, authority, stops, stages, acceptance, and evidence meaning come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root. Lowering, forks, weak bundles, and Dreamer semantics come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root. Storage and recovery identities come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUST-STORAGE#root. The runtime and economics gates remain authoritative for admission and live effects. @status:spec/plan
ZAP: change complexity, value, and Owner threshold
1. Mandatory assessment before semantic change

Every semantic plan change is assessed before admission using its actual immutable typed payloads, incremental complexity, downstream cost, value, necessity, alternatives, and uncertainty. Hashes bind those payloads but do not replace them in the assessment. The trusted application service and runtime enforce the gate rather than prompt wording. Unassessed or stale public mutation is refused. Pure simulation and historical replay remain non-authoritative and perform no external effect. Economics never grants authority withheld by the charter, stop policy, graph, or ordinary action route. @status:spec/plan

Semantic changes include outcome adoption or pivot, obligation disposition or ownership change, semantic lowering, material task-contract replacement, dependency-changing work revision, and creating, transferring, or making a deferral inapplicable. A transition to dropped, superseded, or deferred is semantic; ordinary progress among planned, ready, active, candidate, accepted, and blocked states is not. Draft proposals remain data. Display-only rename, transport or source observation, acceptance of newly produced proof, reuse of immutable currently applicable proof, and capability-specific rendering of an unchanged admitted contract are not semantic plan changes. A registry classifies exact typed payloads rather than prose heuristics; changed meaning cannot be disguised as rendering. @status:spec/plan

A semantic Lowering revision enters this gate once for its exact affected envelope. Subsequent packet and client renders that prove the same semantic-contract identity, RelevantBasis, obligations, dependencies, stage debt, deferrals, and acceptance do not create a fresh allowance or decision. Any changed meaning, affected closure, or team-capacity assumption is reassessed under the ordinary rules. @status:spec/plan

The immutable imported plan and initial intent/outcome envelope exactly bound by the active Owner charter are the approved baseline and do not require redundant change approval. One exact approved proposal envelope covers its ordered product effects while their relevant causal basis remains current. Retained baseline work is not charged as new scope. Changed payload, subject, relevant source or contract, affected closure, cost forecast, team-capacity model, outcome, policy, or typed subject fingerprint cannot reuse the assessment or decision. The semantic node fingerprint retains structural dependencies, ownership, contracts, validation generations, terminal defer/drop/supersede state, and material proof or knowledge, while excluding display-only titles, active job/attempt/event metadata, and ordinary planned/ready/active/candidate/accepted/blocked execution progress. Economics events, hold receipts, prior effects in the same envelope, and unrelated progress do not stale it merely by advancing a global revision. @status:spec/plan

Global revisions and whole-plan hashes are audit provenance, not automatic staleness. Admission compares an exact relevant basis containing active policy, charter, intent/outcome, affected obligations and work, contracts, sources, relevant knowledge, applicability, fog, dependencies, consumers, proof, and configured team assumptions. Every alternative contains full immutable typed effect payloads. Deterministic ordered simulation binds each effect relevant-before and relevant-after fingerprint, so prior effects advance the same envelope while economics records and unrelated progress are excluded. A changed affected input or causal order stales it. @status:spec/plan

Existing MUP imports and historical zap/1 events replay without retroactive assessment. On the first supported estimation or semantic-change attempt, and only after the exact initial charter intent and outcome are active, an internal baseline-boundary event records the accepted committed prefix and active charter. Reads and service construction remain pure. Events at or before that prefix remain history; later semantic changes require admission. The economics projection is lazy and replay performs no estimation or approval. Pure detached simulation creates no authority or external effect. The package remains the 1.0.0 prototype until a separate release decision changes that status. @status:spec/plan
2. Incremental cost and bounded uncertainty

Cost covers new work, redo, and downstream consequences attributable to the proposal relative to the captured approved baseline. It includes implementation, verification, migration, documentation, invalidated-proof revalidation, dependencies and consumers, operations and maintenance, and bounded fog uncertainty. Previously approved retained work and sunk cost are identified but excluded from the new authorization denominator. The same consequence is not charged twice through both its direct task and a summary row. @status:spec/plan

The threshold metric is expected elapsed time to a verified result under a captured meaningful team-capacity model. That model binds configured executor classes, relevant capabilities, nominal parallel capacity, resource capacities, and explicit scheduling assumptions. Transient free-slot or queue churn does not stale it. The Owner-confirmed default is 4 hours and approval is required only above that value. The elapsed interval and critical-path basis, passive waiting, and total agent-hours are separate. Estimates are coarse and evidence-based rather than manufactured precision. @status:spec/plan

Every assessment addresses implementation, verification, migration, documentation, proof revalidation, dependencies and consumers, operations and maintenance, passive external wait, and bounded fog uncertainty as included, not applicable with reason, or unknown. Category rows record agent-effort bounds, elapsed contribution, qualitative consequence, assumptions, and evidence. Overlapping elapsed contributions are not summed. Passive wait affects time to verified result but is not mislabeled as engineering complexity. Proof invalidation covers reproduction on changed inputs; consumer cost includes integration, rollout, compatibility, and rollback; operations cost includes durable maintenance. @status:spec/plan

Uncertainty is expressed as named questions with lower and upper bounds when defensible, materiality, and the cheapest resolution action. An unbounded or threshold-crossing unknown is not converted to zero or false precision. Estimation itself has configurable elapsed and agent-hour budgets. When the budget is exhausted, the assessment stops with explicit unknowns and follows the configured conservative rule rather than entering endless analysis. @status:spec/plan

The assessor states the baseline, proposed effects, included incremental work, excluded retained baseline, and excluded sunk costs. A cheaper alternative is estimated against the same baseline. Migration, documentation, or proof work already required by the baseline remains baseline; only proposal-caused additions or redo are charged. A proposal may not appear cheap by omitting consumers, invalidated evidence, or ongoing operations. @status:spec/plan

Material new evidence, completed effects, changed relevant inputs, or changed configured team assumptions append a forecast revision against the original approved baseline. It records cumulative attributable actual elapsed time, proposal-caused passive wait, and agent-hours separately from remaining intervals and total time to verified result. Progress never resets remaining work to a fresh four-hour allowance and sunk cost never argues for continuation. When the refreshed total crosses the threshold, becomes conservatively unknown, or changes scope, the next unconsumed semantic effect requires new adjudication and exact Owner decision when applicable. The forecast adjudication atomically creates a hold when an initially automatic change first crosses that boundary; an existing hold is explicitly retained, expanded without shrinkage, or superseded by a linked no-smaller successor. Incidental quota, provider overload, resource contention, or Owner pause is an operational wait rather than proposal complexity; wall-clock passage alone does not re-gate the change. @status:spec/plan
3. Value, necessity, and alternatives

A change is classified as mandatory problem resolution, obligatory safeguard, or optional improvement. Mandatory and safeguard classes name the active obligation, constraint, defect, or verified risk that makes them necessary. A difficult safeguard cannot be relabeled optional to avoid its cost, and an attractive optional feature cannot claim a mandatory class without evidence and an applicable obligation. @status:spec/plan

The default comparison records utility and cost separately. Utility dimensions are Owner benefit, risk reduction, urgency, strategic optionality, reversibility, and confidence. Cost derives separate elapsed, engineering-burden, consequence, and uncertainty bands. Overall cost is the conservative maximum of engineering burden, consequence, and uncertainty; the elapsed band remains separate because it controls approval. No rule subtracts hours from utility, mixes unlike units, or presents an arbitrary decimal score as truth. Owner-calibrated dimensionless weights may rank utility alternatives but never alter the elapsed threshold. @status:spec/plan

Let T be the active elapsed threshold and P the configured nominal parallelism. Elapsed cost is negligible at zero, low through T/4, moderate above T/4 through T, high above T through 2T, and critical above 2T or when unbounded. Engineering burden uses the same ratios for agent-hours against T multiplied by P. Consequence is the maximum included category consequence. Uncertainty is negligible when absent, low within one below-threshold band, moderate across adjacent below-threshold bands, high when its upper bound crosses T, and critical when unbounded or materially unknowable. Overall qualitative cost is the maximum of engineering burden, consequence, and uncertainty; elapsed remains the separate approval metric. @status:spec/plan

Every assessment includes the proposal, factual cheaper alternatives considered, and a no-op or continue-baseline alternative. Each alternative states whether it actually solves the mandatory problem and which obligations, guarantees, benefits, and consequences it preserves or sacrifices. An imaginary cheaper option is not evidence. If a valid lower-cost alternative supplies the same mandatory result, it is preferred or the difference is explained. @status:spec/plan

The decision table is total. Invalid or materially incomplete evidence with no defensible recommendation yields investigate_unknown and blocked. Optional negligible utility yields continue_baseline and blocked. Optional low utility is eligible only with negligible or low bounded cost; moderate utility only with negligible, low, or moderate bounded cost; high or critical utility remains substantively eligible with any bounded cost. An eligible undominated proposal yields take_proposal and automatic, while an undominated cheaper executable alternative yields prefer_alternative. Mandatory problems and safeguards choose the least-cost feasible alternative only when it preserves the same obligations; if the proposal is the only evidenced feasible solver, it remains the recommendation. Any selected executable recommendation above threshold or conservatively unknown retains that recommendation and receives owner_decision_required. Necessity never bypasses Owner approval. @status:spec/plan

Money, time, or proof already spent does not make continuation valuable by itself and is not counted again as proposal cost. Reusable artifacts and applicable evidence may reduce incremental cost only when their continued suitability is validated. Switching cost and abandonment consequences are future attributable costs and remain visible. @status:spec/plan
4. Configurable threshold and exact Owner decision

The built-in policy compares expected elapsed hours with the Owner-confirmed threshold of 4.0 hours for the configured team model. Exactly 4.0 is not above the threshold; more than 4.0 requires approval. The team model captures evidenced executor classes, capabilities, nominal parallelism, resource capacities, and scheduling assumptions rather than transient free slots. Policy may configure another positive threshold, qualitative weights, estimation maxima, and conservative unknown handling only through an exact campaign-matching Owner credential decision. @status:spec/plan

A structurally valid selected alternative with defensible but threshold-crossing, unbounded, or policy-unknown cost retains its substantive recommendation and receives owner_decision_required plus a hold over its unknown impact boundary. Invalid or materially incomplete evidence with no defensible recommendation yields investigate_unknown and blocked, with no trusted change hold. For unknown impact, only work proved independent by complete captured dependency closure may continue; stricter policy may hold all starts. No mode treats unknown cost or impact as below threshold. @status:spec/plan

The Owner records approve_exact_proposal, reject_and_continue_baseline, request_revision_and_hold, or defer_decision through the authenticated campaign-matching credential channel; host role or actor text is insufficient. Approval binds the assessment, latest forecast, active policy, scoped relevant basis, selected alternative, and its ordered full-payload effect fingerprints. Rejection preserves baseline. Revision requires a new assessment while the hold persists. Deferral grants no product action. @status:spec/plan

When the same prepared live scope change needs a charter amendment and an above-threshold economics decision, one authenticated Owner response may bind both exact revisions and their common ordered effect envelope. The response separately records both decisions and satisfies neither if its scope or basis differs. An earlier instruction to explore, add, or remove a goal does not approve a cost assessment that did not yet exist. @status:spec/plan

One approval may cover an ordered multi-command envelope, so each command does not ask again. Each effect contains its immutable typed payload, payload hash, subject IDs, predecessor IDs, and expected relevant-basis hashes before and after deterministic simulation. The service admits only the next unconsumed effect when its scoped precondition matches, then records causal advancement. Economics, hold, and unrelated progress events do not enter that basis. Changed payload, relevant scope, input, estimate, team model, or causal order stales the envelope. Economics approval never suppresses CAS, stop, source, authority, obligation, graph, or acceptance checks. @status:spec/plan

Trusted deterministic adjudication may admit a recommended below-threshold change without Owner decision when cost and impact are bounded and policy permits it. The immutable payloads and simulated scoped basis make the value and impact assessment inspectable before admission. A producer-authored assessment cannot admit itself. Optional low-value rejection, needs_evidence, and owner_decision_required remain explicit outcomes. The service records exact economics admission before the product event. @status:spec/plan
5. Pending decisions and live-work reconciliation

When trusted assessment or cumulative-forecast adjudication selects an executable recommendation with owner_decision_required, the same atomic event creates a durable hold over affected work and dependent starts. Compared but unselected expensive alternatives, continue-baseline, investigate-unknown, untrusted drafts, dormant forks, and detached DreamBranches create no hold. Affected dispatch, verification, and conflicting semantic plan application are refused by service and runtime. Work with complete proof of independence continues unless an Owner pause applies. @status:spec/plan

Simulation may calculate hypothetical impact and cost but cannot select a live executable effect, consume approval, alter readiness, drain a job, or create a hold. Rejection and abandonment preserve assessment history without turning the unselected alternative into required work. A later live promotion performs current assessment and admission against its exact base. @status:spec/plan

When affected closure is incomplete, the default hold includes the known closure and every start not proved independent of its unknown boundary. This is conservative without automatically claiming a campaign pause. Policy may choose a stricter all-starts hold. The journal distinguishes a change hold from an Owner stop, resource wait, and campaign completion. @status:spec/plan

Affected in-flight jobs receive durable reconciliation and cooperative stop requests. Stop delivery, process termination, declared safe boundary, and external-effect reconciliation remain separate facts. PID exit or a stop signal is not safe-state proof. Request IDs and receipts survive restart and do not duplicate a process or stop request. Independent in-flight work continues unless it conflicts with the held closure or a broader Owner pause. @status:spec/plan

A campaign-wide Owner pause always dominates a change hold and its release. Scoped Owner pauses also block matching actions. Economics decisions cannot acknowledge, clear, or bypass a pause. Result collection and proposal preparation remain allowed under the existing control rules. @status:spec/plan

On exact approval, the hold remains until all approved commands are applied or explicitly reconciled and affected jobs are safe under the new plan. Rejection before any product effect is rejected_baseline and returns safely stopped work to the unchanged baseline through explicit retry or readiness events. Rejection after a renewed forecast preserves the exact nonempty committed causal prefix as rejected_remaining and rejects only the unapplied suffix; it never claims rollback to the original baseline. Revision or deferral keeps the hold. Attempt and stop history remains, and unresolved, out-of-order, or extra effects keep the hold for reconciliation rather than silent release. @status:spec/plan
6. Enforcement, observability, and acceptance

The application service is the authoritative supported public-mutation gate. It classifies typed event variants, resolves the explicit economics reference, validates the stored adjudication or credentialed Owner decision, and compares only the scoped relevant basis for the next ordered effect. The effect carries its immutable validated payload and prebound product event identity; hashes bind rather than replace it. Official Engine, CLI, HTTP, agent, host, and model mutation routes cannot bypass the gate. Low-level raw journal access is outside the supported authority boundary and this mechanism does not claim OS isolation. Pure apply, simulation, tests, and historical replay grant no authorization. @status:spec/plan

The runtime consults change holds before selection, claim, submit, verification, semantic plan application, and readiness advancement. It performs safe drain and resumption through durable events and continues work proved independent. It refreshes forecasts at material checkpoints without resetting the original baseline or remaining denominator. A runtime omission cannot authorize a public command because the service repeats the gate. @status:spec/plan

The projection exposes policy, assessments, category estimates, passive wait, uncertainty, alternatives, recommendation, Owner decision, envelope simulation and consumption, holds, drain/safe-state receipts, cost-forecast revisions, staleness, and final disposition. Forecasts retain cumulative attributable actual cost and remaining cost against the original approved baseline; they do not reset remaining hours after progress. Viewer explanations distinguish expected elapsed time, passive wait, and agent-hours. Opening a record performs no new estimate or model call. @status:spec/plan

The shared campaign completion predicate refuses closure while a selected economic change awaits an Owner decision, an approved effect remains unconsumed or unreconciled, a change hold remains active, a forecast is unresolved, or an associated external outcome is unknown. Scheduler and direct service or CLI closure use the same predicate. Dormant, hypothetical, rejected, and compared-but-unselected alternatives do not block unrelated closure. @status:spec/plan

Pure economics modules own exact schemas, full effect bundles, scoped fingerprints, team assumptions, cost bands, utility comparison, forecast validation, simulation, and projections. Control owns credential-only policy and Owner decisions. The application service adds a private service-internal event route, explicit economics-reference resolution, durable effect reservation, retry, and causal consumption. Runtime hold adapters reuse the established reconciliation and safe-drain validators. CLI/backend expose proposal, simulation, decision, status, and explanation. Estimator requests, responses, waits, and staleness are durable proposal-only effects outside reducers and can never self-admit. Domain and knowledge provide read-only affected fingerprints and closure. @status:spec/plan

Acceptance evidence covers actual-payload assessment, scoped basis unaffected by economics events or unrelated progress, ordered causal advancement, meaningful team-capacity changes, threshold boundaries, passive wait versus engineering burden, mandatory and safeguard classification, optional low-value rejection, high-value adoption, no acceptable cheaper alternative, no-op comparison, unknown modes, estimation-budget exhaustion, attributable baseline and sunk-cost exclusion, forecast crossing, stale approval, multi-command consumption, historical replay, semantic drop, supersede and defer, semantic lowering versus pure rendering, affected holds, independent progress, safe drain and restart, Owner-pause precedence, rejection release, partial-application recovery, public-gate bypass refusal, pure simulation, combined Owner decisions, shared closure refusal, and large-plan attribution. Required scenarios include a high-value optional six-hour change that remains take_proposal with owner_decision_required, a sole feasible mandatory six-hour fix that remains recommended but cannot execute without exact Owner approval, and a costly low-value optional change that continues the baseline without a hold. @status:spec/plan
7. Permanent references

Outcome and plan meaning come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root and spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-ADAPTIVE-CYCLE#root. Data, provenance, replay, and viewer obligations come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root. Trusted service, runtime, recovery, and backend boundaries come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUNTIME#root. This specification adds a pre-change economics gate without weakening any referenced obligation. @status:spec/plan
ZAP: canonical data, events, and future viewing
1. Data contract and truthful implemented surface

This document defines required ZAP data properties and the path to external tools. The legacy container format is schema zap/1 and preserves the complete imported MUP plan, task contracts, and separate ZAP extensions. The current Rust store and its explicit epochs follow ZAP-RUST-STORAGE.xml; legacy bytes retain their own interpretation. A field in a draft schema does not imply an implemented transition. Every available operation has an explicit contract, handler, and validation; other requirements remain planned. @status:spec/plan

The implemented operation set is published from actual handler, schema, and route registries through capabilities and the command contract. Unknown commands, versions, fields, and rule operators are refused. The CLI and backend do not infer authority from actor labels; dry run and observation are not described as performed or accepted product actions. @status:spec/plan

The historical prototype's five original commands and later migration, charter, capture, snapshot, repair, promotion, automatic coordination, and authenticated backend behavior remain migration and characterization inputs. Rust capabilities count as implemented only when their own registries and evidence publish them. Import and installation do not start NEXT. The interactive canvas, IDE plugin, and a custom IDE are outside this package. @status:spec/plan

The Rust MVP must represent StrategicPlan and Lowering revisions, obligations and stage debt, forks, capabilities and desired or resolved profiles, packet and attempt lineage, claims, DispatchIntents and ExternalJobHandles, liveness and checkpoints, WeakBundles and encounter journals, DreamBranches, economics, holds, stop state, completion blockers, and their provenance. Planned schema text is not implementation evidence. @status:spec/plan

Personal execution progress belongs to a ZAP context bound to the user and exact checkout. Shared requirements, accepted project facts, code, evidence, and intentionally shared campaign inputs remain in the repository. No shared queue of personal sessions is created. The pilot imports a separate copy of the seed and task contracts; it does not rewrite MUP plan.toml, settings, GOAL, statuses, or active constraints. @status:spec/plan
2. Immutable base and meaning-preserving import

The initial base preserves source files with hashes of exact bytes, source names, and captured identities. The parsed model is bound to that base. New changes are append-only events; the base is not rewritten under a new interpretation. Projections and acceleration snapshots derive from a specific base and accepted event sequence. @status:spec/plan

In the legacy prototype format, base.json with schema zap/1 contains the complete MUP plan, task contracts, and raw captures with base64 source bytes and SHA-256. events.jsonl begins with store.imported, binding the journal to the base hash. Later rows carry seq, revision, previous_revision, event_id, kind, reason, payload, and command_sha256. Commands use base_revision; the ZAP projection revision is separate from the imported plan revision. These are legacy local-store names; the Rust store and implemented HTTP interface have separate public contracts. @status:spec/plan

Import preserves every mandate, node, identity, order, hierarchy, dependency, state, acceptance criterion, evidence item, task, and unknown source-format extension. Values are not guessed from titles or simplified during conversion. Type and representation changes have explicit source mappings; retained source bytes allow later verification of material not yet interpreted. @status:spec/plan

The known NEXT pilot expects 425 nodes and 212 task contracts at the captured source state. Individual identities, values, links, and contract contents are verified; matching two counts is insufficient. New work_type, maturity, and knowledge annotations are separate and may remain unspecified. Prior acceptance is preserved as a sourced imported assertion, not a new ZAP verification. @status:spec/plan

Imported Owner commands and decisions retain provenance and require explicit charter-preparation classification. Deserialization neither loses them nor makes them executable. The NEXT start prohibition, D-022, and external-action constraints remain visible. Import cannot create activation evidence; a source file owner field is not a trusted control channel. @status:spec/plan
3. Domain graph and evidence provenance

Intent, expected-outcome revisions, value and feasibility assessments, mandates, obligations, work, facts, decisions, unknown regions, approaches, and evidence have stable identities. Renaming does not change identity, and identity is not reused for another subject. Node kind, state, work purpose, delivery route, declared maturity, achieved stage, current value, and knowledge applicability are independent. A declared classification proves no stage, and child count proves no parent acceptance. @status:spec/plan

Relations show which requirement work serves, which sources support a conclusion, which evidence supports a claim, which premises a decision uses, and what it changes. Contradiction, replacement, and invalidation preserve prior records. A relation needs defined endpoints and clear meaning; similar wording does not create a dependency. @status:spec/plan

Normative fact text and specification status remain separate from current-state observations and accepted evidence. An observation names the measured subject, method, and applicability. A conclusion references its premises. Acceptance lists proven obligations and required check results. A link, confident prose, or third-party PASS does not raise status. @status:spec/plan

A source reference contains a stable handle, location or spec anchor, source kind, and captured content identity. Verification also binds inputs, dependencies, fixtures, command, toolchain, target, and environment. A URL or commit without that scope is not reproducibility. An unavailable source remains unresolved rather than verified. @status:spec/plan

unexamined, bounded, evidenced, and invalidated apply to a specific unknown region and question. An authorized scope exclusion is stored separately. A closed graph does not prove absolute knowledge completeness. Missing links and assessments remain unknown; an empty set is not proof of no risk. @status:spec/plan

Changed captured source content marks dependent evidence and conclusions for reassessment without erasing acceptance history or invalidating unrelated results. The graph identifies known impact; the coordinator assesses whether recorded dependencies are semantically complete. Incomplete input closure requires affected verification, not an automatic full product run. @status:spec/plan

A lowering result binds to an expected-outcome revision and maps its obligations to child work, evidence, and integration acceptance. Each deferral has a concrete scope and obligation. Outcome revision records each prior obligation disposition, successor, remaining difference, and authority. Readiness uses required intermediate guarantees: an accepted experiment is not a finished interface. Missing coverage remains a defect even when every created task is done. @status:spec/plan

Lowering, packet, logical operation, attempt, message, artifact, evidence, verification, and acceptance have separate stable identities and causal relations. A packet digest protects bytes but does not replace packet_id, parent Lowering revision, semantic-contract identity, render profile, or derived_from and supersedes lineage. A rerender or retry does not erase earlier candidates or receipts. @status:spec/plan

A strategic fork, DreamBranch, execution workspace, and source-control branch are different subjects. Dream data binds a live base revision and stores only its proposed delta, assumptions, questions, estimates, and calculated effects. It remains detached from live scope, work, approval consumption, and holds until an exact authorized application event. @status:spec/plan
3a. Current adaptive-review contract

A review has review_id, a link to the prior material review, input signals, and captures of base hash, ZAP revision or cursor, intent, charter, prior outcome, route, material sources, and affected jobs. Transition acceptance checks every material input for currency. Journal CAS alone does not prove an external service unchanged or a worker stopped. An ordinary session change does not require a review. @status:spec/plan

The record contains unknown-region changes before and after, newly found questions, source dependencies, affected conclusion closure, and an assessment of closure completeness. It preserves comparable alternatives and grounded or unknown assessments of Owner value, feasibility under named conditions, remaining cost, and risk. Historical truth, current applicability, and present value are distinct. An incomplete map is not presented as exhaustive analysis. @status:spec/plan

A decision binds the selected alternative, concise rationale, actual authority, before and after outcome revisions, tradeoffs, and preserved benefit. The transition lists affected-obligation dispositions, task, contract, dependency, priority, acceptance, and deferral changes, preserved evidence, and a live-job plan. Stop-rule assessment, expected revision, and command identity are separate. Proposal, accepted transition, and confirmed job effect are distinct states. A meaningful keep-route decision records its basis without artificial plan change. @status:spec/plan

The viewer shows original intent, prior and current expected outcomes, preserved benefit, tradeoffs, unmet properties, and reasons priorities changed. Fog expansion, stale premises, the next experiment, and reversibility remain visible. Results distinguish original success, authorized revised success, partial benefit, and unattainability under known conditions. Stored decisions and transitions supply this view; the viewer does not invent it with a new model call. @status:spec/plan

The adaptive cycle has separate intent, outcome, and review proposals and policy-admitted application events. It preserves stale captures, essential obligations, evidence applicability, and live-job reconciliation. The command contract and capabilities list only actual event types; a proposal is not application. @status:spec/plan
4. Commands, journal, and deterministic replay

A data-changing command names the logical object, expected base or projection revision, request identity, and causal references. The receiver validates operation support, inputs, preconditions, and separate required authority. A stale revision yields an explicit conflict for rereading instead of overwriting unknown changes. Data idempotency does not make repetition of an external effect safe. @status:spec/plan

One idempotency key identifies one logical command and its content. An exact retry returns the known result without another transition; different content under the key is refused. The key is not replaced to repeat an operation with unknown outcome. Recovery uses receipts, external-operation identity, and actual postconditions when supported. @status:spec/plan

Accepted changes form an ordered append-only sequence with event identities, revisions, and causal references. An operation records its whole defined transition or leaves a detectable incomplete tail. The format distinguishes complete events from a partial last row; the parser does not ignore middle corruption or treat a partial tail as a completed command. @status:spec/plan

The kernel composes explicit core, control, domain, knowledge, and runtime handler registries. Every extension event belongs to exactly one data, action, or trusted-observation route; internal control events are unavailable to public callers. Replay uses the same registry and reproduces admitted history without reauthentication or external effects. @status:spec/plan

Recovery finds the last complete confirmed boundary, preserves corruption evidence, and reconciles the related command result. Damaged bytes are not silently deleted to make replay pass. Explicit storage mechanisms define repair and authority. While outcome is ambiguous, no external effect repeats. A plain file does not promise exclusion of arbitrary concurrent writers. @status:spec/plan

One reducer version, immutable base, and confirmed event sequence produce one projection. Replay calls no LLM, network, current clock, executor, or external command. Time, semantic assessments, and observations enter as sourced stored data. Changed computation rules require an explicit version and verified migration; old events are not silently reinterpreted. @status:spec/plan

A snapshot records base identity, reducer version, event boundary, and verifiable projection identity. It accelerates reading and can be rebuilt from canonical data. It neither creates authority nor replaces a missing journal. Identity mismatch requires fetching the correct data rather than joining incompatible fragments. @status:spec/plan

A decision or semantic-condition assessment stores concise rationale, sources, and scope. Replay reproduces its existence and effects without claiming to re-prove language truth. Reassessment on new data creates a new record and may supersede the old conclusion while preserving history. Private reasoning chains are not required journal data. @status:spec/plan
5. Separation of Owner control and editable data

The control service authenticates an opaque credential or configured host principal outside the campaign store and binds role, campaign, and allowed commands. Reader is separate from owner and coordinator; the agent route remains data-only. Secrets do not enter the journal, JSON command, packet, argv, or environment. This boundary does not claim protection from an OS administrator or same-user process already able to read protected configuration. @status:spec/plan

The journal may store a verified reference to an accepted Owner command and its effects. Provenance is checked through the control boundary; editing its textual projection does not create new authority. Schema validation alone is insufficient. A successful rule assessment does not prove stop delivery to every executor. @status:spec/plan

Condition assessment, the whole-campaign stop decision, prevention of new launches, and actual safe state of running jobs are observed separately. Unfinished jobs remain visible during a stop. Result collection and preparation for an Owner decision are visible authorized completion work; a third architectural attempt cannot be hidden inside those records. @status:spec/plan

needs_evidence is the explicit result of missing assessment inputs. Expression evaluation preserves unknown according to declared operator logic and refuses unsupported operators. The executor investigates required data without launching the conditionally blocked action. Unknown is not serialized as false, an empty string, or an absent rule. @status:spec/plan

evaluate-stop accepts only an unapproved zap-stop/1 example with status example_unapproved. A rule has id, when, run scope, and timing before_action or before_next_action; semantic values are true, false, or null. failed_approaches with gte 2 finds two confirmed failures for any one problem in campaign history. The result analyzes an example and neither activates runtime policy nor authorizes an action. A late check reports too_late. @status:spec/plan

Resume binds the exact active pause ID and hash, separately verified delivery and actual-safe-state acknowledgements, and an Owner credential. A one-shot exception binds one action identity, payload, and source set. Only the Owner changes an approach epoch; history remains. @status:spec/plan
6. Campaigns, sessions, and actual execution

Campaign state describes obligations and controlled work progress; a session is current coordinator context; a run or job is a concrete execution with observed results. Their identities and completion reasons are separate. Closing a window or lacking narration does not finish a job; job completion does not accept an obligation; resource wait is neither policy pause nor campaign completion. @status:spec/plan

A resource record names the unavailable capability, observation, affected operations, and known retry condition. Unknown recovery time remains explicit. Background waiting and wakeup are shown only when an authorized runtime is actually configured. Session changes preserve attempts, approaches, and evidence; secrets and full sensitive provider responses stay out of the journal. @status:spec/plan

After acceptance, durable project knowledge receives a permanent repository source; the local record retains its acceptance provenance. Personal settings, unfinished reasoning, machine facts, and local campaign progress are not published automatically. Data from another worker or documentation repository is read through a captured source and agreed ownership rather than a shared status string. @status:spec/plan
7. Future viewer and machine interface

Owner clarification of 2026-09-13: the future viewer is a full interactive canvas for a large graph with convenient navigation. Selected-node content is read in place without losing graph position. Three.js is a proposed rendering candidate; engine and dimensionality are selected during viewer implementation from capability and measurement. The Rust MVP data contract must support this future client; the application remains separate work. @status:spec/plan

The canvas supports pan and zoom, search with result focus, hierarchy and dependency navigation, collapse and expansion, filters, navigation history, and saved viewpoints. Overview and detail use the same stable IDs. New events and renames do not reset selection or position. Camera, panels, and bookmarks are view state, not mandate or acceptance changes. @status:spec/plan

The selected-node inspector shows available full content: work goal and steps, criteria and checks, sources, related specifications, facts, decisions and reasons, evidence, dependencies, maturity, deferrals, and change history. A summary does not replace the detailed contract; unavailable content is explicit. Following a related node preserves context. Text loads through verified source handles, not an arbitrary path from untrusted task prose. @status:spec/plan

Every material canvas entity—a node, edge, known or unknown region, job, or decision—opens assembled detail in place. The response includes available content, provenance, and history, and distinguishes missing, unloaded, unavailable, and stale data. The backend does not invent explanations for data gaps and preserves selected-entity identity. @status:spec/plan

The backend provides separate overview or subgraph, search, node-detail, dependency, revision-comparison, readiness, why, packet, and resume queries with stable identities, revision, scope, completeness, and cursor. Large graphs load incrementally while keeping every result reachable. Unloaded, filtered, unavailable, excluded, and semantically unknown regions are distinct. Clustering and levels of detail do not rewrite the canonical plan or require a model call for navigation. @status:spec/plan

The Owner proposed Heroes 3 and StarCraft as the interface metaphor: explored map, research frontier, and fog beyond it. Known areas are clear and saturated; transparency, saturation, boundaries, and optional fog show transition to the unknown. Unknown detail is not painted as existing nodes. A colorful center suggests explored territory but camera proximity does not prove knowledge; known areas may still contain gaps or stale data. ZAP creates its own graphics and symbols; game names are experience references, not assets to copy. @status:spec/plan

Additional Owner clarification of 2026-09-13: the visual style is game-like with an explicit Heroes 3 reference. It envisions a vivid illustrated map, recognizable objects and icons, styled paths, fog, and game-like detail panels. Beauty, clarity of important signals, and readability are joint criteria. Decorative layers preserve graph and text legibility across scales; a usable inspector shows the full node contract. This future canvas art direction remains separate from the current backend. @status:spec/plan

Color, saturation, geometry, outline, icons, edge styling, and text jointly distinguish independent properties. A possible initial mapping uses clarity or fog for knowledge, shape for work purpose, outline and icon for execution state, and edge style for relation meaning. A legend explains the mapping; critical information does not depend on color alone. Labels and inspector remain readable with effects enabled, and motion or decorative fog can be reduced. @status:spec/plan

Both visual and machine data distinguish an unexamined region, bounded research question, evidenced knowledge, information that lost applicability, deliberate scope exclusion, and client data not yet loaded. Fog returning after a fact or goal change is an observed knowledge change, not a loading error. Filtering and collapsing hide a view without changing knowledge or acceptance status. @status:spec/plan

The future viewer may use Qwik 2, but its data contract remains framework-independent. The Rust MVP must implement the machine-data and event backend; the canvas app, IDE plugin, and custom IDE remain separate work. Machine inputs and outputs expose strategy, work, facts, decisions, unknown regions, evidence, approaches, stages, debt, packets, runtime, economics, and stop reasons without treating prose as protocol. Semantic properties are separate from rendering colors, geometry, and camera position. @status:spec/plan

A client receives a snapshot with campaign, base, schema, revision, and last-included-event cursor identity. Continuation references that cursor and sequence. A cursor is journal position, not wall-clock time. Duplicate events are recognized by identity; foreign base, gap, or unknown cursor requires an explicit gap response and an appropriate snapshot. @status:spec/plan

The authenticated backend serves snapshot and resumable event tail or SSE under one base, revision, and cursor identity. Page cursors bind query and revision. Gaps, foreign bases, and stale pages are explicit. A pending final fragment is visible to a reader as the committed-state diagnostic boundary but blocks mutations; middle corruption is not masked. @status:spec/plan

The external surface includes plan-change, decision, invalidation, rule-assessment, campaign-pause, resource-wait, worker-result, acceptance, and fact-promotion events. Implemented registries and capabilities are authoritative for actual families, wire identifiers, and versions. An unknown type is never presented as a successfully applied transition. @status:spec/plan

The viewer shows stored rationale and source references. Opening an item does not trigger new semantic assessment or rewrite an event. A composite conclusion exposes premises, applicability, assessment authorship, and current evidence validity. Artifact maturity, producer assertion, and central acceptance remain visibly distinct. @status:spec/plan

Machine views expose every public state and material diagnostic needed to explain strategy and execution lineage, source and proof applicability, lowering, stages and debt, packet context and omissions, forks and dreams, role routing, native dispatch, liveness, retries, resources, economics, holds, stops, completion blockers, and invalidation. Missing data is labeled rather than reconstructed through an implicit model call, and secrets remain outside projections. @status:spec/plan

Human explanations introduce required concepts before use and connect them to the reader's goal. Overview, step-by-step explanation, and source evidence are separate projections. A shorter explanation does not delete obligations or grounds from canonical data, and editing does not require an Owner stop after each passage. @status:spec/plan

Future IDE actions use typed commands, stable IDs, captured source handles, and expected revision. Renaming changes display text while preserving identity; opening a source does not guess a path from a title. A control action checks backend authority; a button or editable JSON is not an Owner-activation channel. A read-only viewer can operate without command capability. @status:spec/plan

Future viewer verification covers projection equivalence between full replay and snapshot plus tail, duplicates, gaps, partial tail, stale revision, unknown type, and an unperformed Owner command. It verifies truthful distinctions among pause, resource wait, running job, and accepted task. These scenarios neither run NEXT nor replace final campaign verification. @status:spec/plan
