A lowering request binds the strategic revision, target branch, executor capabilities, captured facts and source identities, RelevantBasis, delegated choices, required maturity, known risks, and unresolved horizons. The result contains versioned work contracts, dependencies, traceability, verification duties, integration ownership, prepared forks, and refinement triggers. @status:spec/plan

The kernel validates identities, references, obligation coverage, dependencies, authority, source closure, write and resource conflicts, stage duties, and deferral dispositions. These checks prove declared structural conservation, not semantic sufficiency. A Senior assesses faithfulness for architecture or meaning changes, and later evidence establishes actual satisfaction. @status:spec/plan

Every active obligation and every undischarged prototype, functional-MVP, and productization duty maps to executable work, verification and integration, a named successor, or an authorized inapplicability disposition. Every deferral retains scope, reason, present guarantees, owner, and closure obligation. Refinement, priority change, task deletion, or packet rendering cannot erase debt, history, unmet differences, or consumer obligations. @status:spec/plan

Semantic lowering creates or changes meaning-bearing work contracts, dependencies, ownership, obligation dispositions, stages, or deferrals and therefore follows adaptive and economics admission. Rendering an unchanged admitted contract for a different model, context window, harness, or presentation is derived and does not require another economic decision. A renderer proves semantic-contract identity and preserved debt; changed meaning cannot be labeled rendering to evade admission. @status:spec/plan

Normal execution lowers the nearest valuable frontier until an executor can understand an action and a sufficient check is inexpensive. Distant work stays coarse with inherited obligations, known material forks, and a refinement trigger. A sealed offline envelope lowers as far as present knowledge permits and represents an unknown architectural boundary as a diagnostic task, admissible alternatives, and return condition rather than invented exact steps. @status:spec/plan

A changed strategy, source, contract, policy, capability, or resource marks only affected lowerings and packet renders stale according to captured dependencies and semantic fingerprints. A global event counter, unrelated progress, or economics record does not invalidate an otherwise applicable packet. Applicable artifacts, observations, and proof are retained subject to evidence applicability. @status:spec/plan
3. Strategic forks and prepared weak-model choices

A material fork has stable identity and records its problem, facts and unknowns, alternatives, preconditions, expected value and cost, hazards, recommendation and rationale, selection authority, rejection conditions, and next diagnostic action. Important forks remain visible in strategy and are projected into lowerings and packets when relevant. @status:spec/plan

An executor selects a prepared fork only while its preconditions and delegated authority remain current. True, false, and unknown conditions remain distinct; unknown requests the named evidence. If no prepared option fits, the executor records an encounter and requests refinement, while any separately authorized diagnostic or independent work may continue. @status:spec/plan

An unselected strategic alternative is a dormant option. It is not an obligation, queued task, failed approach, selected economic change, or hold. Switching routes preserves rejected and abandoned alternatives, evidence, reasons, and attempt history and cannot reset an Owner stop counter. @status:spec/plan
4. Strong-plan and weak-execution round trip

A WeakBundle export binds its exact strategic and Lowering revisions, packet set, capability profile, required rules and sources, source closure and omissions, prepared forks and recommendations, delegated decisions, acceptance, stop conditions, content identities, and explicit export scope. It contains no cloud credential and requires no live registry, external model, or source-host connection for bounded local use. @status:spec/plan

Offline execution appends stable records for attempts, candidates, selected branches, observations, contradictions, unavailable capabilities, failed methods, unresolved questions, checks, artifacts, and effects. These are returned facts and proposals, not canonical acceptance or authority. A judgment beyond the prepared capability or decision envelope becomes awaiting refinement or a capability wait. @status:spec/plan

A return bundle contains the delta since export and referenced evidence. Import verifies base identity, packet and attempt lineage, artifact hashes, and idempotency, then reconciles against the current strategic revision. It classifies returned material as applicable candidate evidence, stale result, contradiction, failure, new unknown, or semantic-change proposal; it never overwrites newer strategy through last-writer-wins. @status:spec/plan

A strong planning environment receives a bounded account of changed assumptions, unresolved decisions, and evidence, reassesses only affected meaning, and emits a new strategic or Lowering revision when warranted. Previous strategy, packets, attempts, findings, and applicable evidence remain inspectable. The initial round trip may use explicit file exchange and does not require distributed consensus. @status:spec/plan

A wholly local installation may use its configured weak model as coordinator for decisions inside the active charter, assigned capability, and prepared decision envelope. It does not fabricate a stronger reviewer or require a cloud round trip after every result. Producer and acceptor identities, evidence requirements, stop rules, and service admission remain unchanged. @status:spec/plan
5. Dreamer exploration and live scope change

The conversational entry distinguishes an explicit live add or remove instruction from requests to imagine, simulate, explore, or plan together. A live instruction prepares an exact semantic proposal. Exploratory language creates a DreamBranch from an exact live revision. When root versus subgoal attachment is materially ambiguous, the system asks one focused placement question rather than guessing. @status:spec/plan

Before admitting a new goal, the system asks whether the Owner wants it grilled. If selected, the grill establishes beneficiary, observable success, essential constraints, non-goals, delegated tradeoffs, and consequential forks. Existing evidence answers factual questions first; Owner questions use plain-language consequences, distinct choices, and a recommendation. Answers, sources, and unresolved questions persist across compaction and are reused until material grounds change. @status:spec/plan

A DreamBranch stores only its delta over a base revision plus assumptions, questions, estimates, alternatives, and calculated effects on dependencies, knowledge, value, evidence, obligations, and lowering. Simulation cannot dispatch work, alter the live frontier, consume live approvals, activate authority, or create an economics hold. Strategic forks, DreamBranches, execution sandboxes, and source-control branches are distinct typed subjects. @status:spec/plan

Application requires an explicit Owner or charter-authorized live command over the exact prepared payload. The service checks the current base, authority, stop state, affected closure, economics, evidence applicability, and live jobs. It reconciles concurrent drift rather than overwriting it. A stale dream stays detached until revised; applicable proof and unaffected work survive. @status:spec/plan

When one prepared scope change requires both a charter amendment and an above-threshold economics decision, one authenticated Owner response may bind both exact revisions and their common effect envelope. An earlier request to explore or add an idea does not approve cost learned later, while one already reviewed envelope is not presented twice for equivalent confirmation. @status:spec/plan

Removing or unzapping a goal records dispositions for its obligations, dependents, evidence, stage debt, artifacts, consumers, deferrals, and outstanding external effects. It cannot erase history or remove a prerequisite still used elsewhere. Achievement of an authorized smaller outcome is reported as revised success, not retrospective completion of the original outcome. @status:spec/plan
6. Adaptation, economics, and stops

Every material live delta uses the adaptive review and change-economics contracts: compute known impact, assess closure completeness and new semantic links, preserve nonmonotonic fog, compare alternatives against the same baseline, and admit only the exact authorized effects. Baseline work is not repeatedly reauthorized, cumulative forecasts cannot be split into fresh allowances, and pure detached simulation remains non-authoritative. @status:spec/plan

A selected executable live change whose expected elapsed time to a verified result is above the active threshold, or whose policy-relevant cost or impact is conservatively unknown, holds affected work and dependent starts. Work with complete proof of independence continues. Dormant forks, DreamBranches, rejected alternatives, and untrusted drafts create no hold. @status:spec/plan

An Owner campaign stop pauses all new campaign work and safely drains in-flight operations regardless of a Dreamer, lowering, or economics state. Proposal preparation and surviving-result collection remain allowed, but no economics decision, branch application, route change, or packet render resumes product work. Resume requires the exact Owner control defined by the active pause contract. @status:spec/plan
7. Permanent references

Intent, obligations, maturity, central acceptance, and Owner stops come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root. Adaptive outcome revision and proof reuse come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-ADAPTIVE-CYCLE#root. Economic admission comes from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-CHANGE-ECONOMICS#root. Packet and host behavior comes from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root. @status:spec/plan
ZAP: agreed intent and sustained autonomous execution
1. Outcome model and current-work boundary

ZAP serves campaigns that, after initial agreement, may run for hours, days, or weeks across sessions and executors. Its goal is a valuable verified result in the sense of Owner intent. New knowledge causes reassessment of uncertainty, value, feasibility, the current expected outcome, and the route. The concrete outcome may change within the authorized tradeoff space; the initial task list is not an immutable goal. Duration is not limited to one task or conversation. This document defines the contract and does not itself authorize execution. @status:spec/plan

ZAP extends lossless planning, central acceptance, focused verification, parallel-work coordination, and multi-user-planning recovery. Permanent foundations are listed in the sources section. It adds an Owner-controlled autonomy charter, a fact graph, and explicit lowering. Publishing or installing the package does not replace a campaign-specific charter. @status:spec/plan

Implemented operations are defined by the actual capabilities registries and machine command contract. The CLI, control service, persistent coordinator, and backend do not enlarge authority: import remains draft, an observation is not acceptance, and unsupported operations are refused. @status:spec/plan

ZAP-authored specifications, public documentation, skills, and examples are written in English. Preserved imported sources and legacy payloads remain byte-faithful, and intentional Unicode fixtures may retain the exact data under test. Protocol identifiers, hashes, addresses, and source captures are never translated. @status:spec/plan

The system owns durable authority, intent, revisions, obligations, decisions, evidence, operations, and recovery state outside model context. Models contribute bounded semantic judgments and candidate artifacts; deterministic services validate admissibility, readiness, lineage, effects, and the next permitted transition. Compaction, process loss, account replacement, or a different model does not create a new campaign or authority. @status:spec/plan

Owner intent and charter, the strategic graph, lowered execution graph, and packet or client projections are linked representations of one versioned model with explicit authority between them. A derived view cannot redefine the desired result. Detailed lowering and packet requirements are defined by spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root and spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root. @status:spec/plan
2. Initial agreement and autonomy charter

The first pass with the Owner defines the valuable final outcome, work boundaries, mandatory properties, priorities, acceptable tradeoffs, and how completion will be verified. The coordinator investigates available facts and asks only intent questions those facts cannot answer. Dependent questions follow their prerequisites; independent research may continue in parallel. @status:spec/plan

An Owner question explains the practical consequence in plain language, offers distinct options, and gives a recommendation with a reason. An unknown fact is not replaced with a convenient answer choice. An accepted decision is reused until material grounds change; asking again must identify what changed. @status:spec/plan

The autonomy charter binds the campaign and initial state to the Owner mandate. It distinguishes required benefit, essential constraints, and admissible approximations; defines delegated technical and priority decisions, reserved decisions, permitted external actions, and stop rules. Outcome hypotheses may change inside this space without renegotiating the charter after every discovery. Resource and recovery settings are recorded where needed; absence of a numeric limit is not replaced with an invented global cap. @status:spec/plan

The Owner controls accepted charter terms separately from the agent-editable plan. An agent may prepare a draft, explanation, or amendment proposal. Changing a task, note, local file, or author field does not create authority. Verifiable Owner-command provenance comes from a trusted control adapter outside agent-editable state. @status:spec/plan

A charter is drafted first; the Owner then explicitly activates the exact revision for the named campaign through the trusted control service. An opaque credential is bound outside the editable store to a role, campaign, and allowed actions. Import, installation, harness mode, and an owner field neither activate the charter nor start the campaign. @status:spec/plan

Charter preparation explicitly classifies every imported constraint as retained unchanged, requiring an Owner decision, or explicitly replaced by the Owner. Import preserves original wording and provenance. For the NEXT pilot this includes the prohibition on starting implementation, NEXT-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY, unresolved D-022, and applicable publication constraints. Unknown classification does not remove a constraint; successful import does not start NEXT. @status:spec/plan

New Owner terms create a new charter revision with rationale and scope; the previous revision remains available. Unstarted proposals are reassessed under the active revision. Started operations are reconciled with it before the next permitted boundary. An agent cannot rewrite an accepted rule or erase a prior trigger to continue work. @status:spec/plan
3. Stop conditions and actual inability to continue

A methodological pause arises from an Owner command or an accepted charter condition. The coordinator adds no mandatory question of its own after every decision, stage, commit, or model change. Existing environment, authority, and tool constraints remain: an impossible or unauthorized action does not become permitted merely to keep work continuous. @status:spec/plan

A rule has a stable identity and revision. Its expression uses explicitly supported operations over typed values, such as logical composition, value comparison, and counts of confirmed outcomes. The evaluator validates the expression and its inputs deterministically. It neither claims arbitrary natural language is algorithmically understood nor executes rule text as code. @status:spec/plan

A semantic condition, such as whether a format change affects user-data migration, receives a separate agent assessment. The record names the proposed action, rule revision, data scope, sources, material basis, and result. The machine may verify the record and evaluate an expression over its result; the semantic conclusion still requires evidence and available verification. The assessment does not acquire Owner authority. @status:spec/plan

Insufficient data for a condition yields needs_evidence. The coordinator investigates the missing fact and does not begin an action whose permission or stop condition is unknown. Unknown is not converted to false or presented as a confirmed trigger. If required evidence is unavailable, the wait and its reason are recorded; this does not invent a stop policy. @status:spec/plan

The Owner-selected default for a triggered condition is a whole-campaign stop. No new task or approach starts. Running executors perform only what is necessary to reach the declared safe boundary and preserve artifacts. Collecting surviving evidence and preparing material for an Owner decision are allowed; continuing product work under the name of preparation is not. Resume follows an Owner command and the active charter revision. @status:spec/plan

A pause persists until an accepted Owner command binds its exact pause ID and current hash. Scoped pauses coexist; a campaign pause dominates. Stop delivery and actual safe state are observed separately. A missing signal, node or session change, or agent explanation does not clear the pause. @status:spec/plan

Resume does not disable later stop conditions. The Owner may permit exactly one prepared action by binding an exception to the rule, pause ID, and command-content identity. Only the Owner may begin a new approach-counting epoch or source cursor; prior history remains. Without that decision an agent does not reset counters or rename the problem to avoid retriggering. @status:spec/plan

An architectural approach is bound to one problem and its source assumptions: its hypothesis, material solution method, and result criterion are named. Repeating a command after overload, fixing a typo, and adding a check to the same solution are not new architectural approaches. Renaming a task, using a new worker, or starting a new session does not reset problem history. Semantic equivalence of attempts receives a reasoned assessment rather than being inferred from matching names. @status:spec/plan

Example Owner rules stop before a public-format change that affects user-data migration and present options after two failed architectural approaches to one problem. Failures are counted per problem across the campaign; failures on different problems do not add together, and changing the current task does not hide earlier outcomes. The campaign reaches a safe boundary, no third approach starts, and reviewing evidence or preparing an option comparison remains allowed. @status:spec/plan

A before-action condition is evaluated against the captured proposal before its effect begins. A check after execution may expose a violation but is recorded as too_late, not as prevention. Changing prepared command content requires reassessment, and a before-next-action threshold does not authorize one more action. @status:spec/plan

An unavailable server, exhausted quota, occupied resource, unknown external outcome, or unavailable evidence is recorded as an actual wait or inability to perform a specific step. It is neither campaign completion nor an Owner-rule trigger. Independent authorized work may continue unless a campaign stop applies; the reason, observed state, and retry condition remain visible. @status:spec/plan
4. Obligations, facts, and unknown regions

ZAP's core objects are Owner intent and charter, expected-outcome revisions, value and feasibility assessments, obligations, work nodes, facts, evidence, decisions, unknown regions, approaches, events, and projections. An obligation states required benefit or a guarantee for an outcome revision; a task is the current way to obtain it. Replacing a method does not erase the obligation. An authorized outcome revision may change applicability only with an explicit disposition and provenance. The graph links grounds to dependent decisions, work, and checks. @status:spec/plan

work_type identifies purpose: evidence, decision, change, verification, or integration. delivery_route is direct or an ordered set of applicable stages. Declared maturity is unspecified, prototype, functional, or productized; achieved maturity separately requires stage evidence and scoped acceptance. These axes are independent of node.kind and execution state. node.classified is only a declared annotation and proves neither maturity nor consumer readiness. Imported names do not infer classification; absence stays explicit. @status:spec/plan

A broad unknown region within the mandate, a precise research question, and a deliberately excluded region are different records. A broad region need only be bounded by the desired result and next refinement trigger; the whole world need not be atomized in advance. Exclusion requires authority and a reason. Lack of knowledge is not exclusion. @status:spec/plan

Knowledge records distinguish an unexamined region, a bounded question, evidence-supported knowledge, invalidated knowledge, and a region currently irrelevant to the selected route. Relevance may change when facts or the outcome change. A source capture identifies content but does not itself prove truth, applicability, or complete dependency closure. @status:spec/plan

A normative fact states a requirement and its specification status. An observation reports measured state of a specific subject; acceptance establishes a specific obligation. A fact marker or impl/done status alone does not prove current code behavior. Sources carry content identity and conclusions show their premises. Uncalibrated model-confidence percentages do not replace evidence. @status:spec/plan

A material decision stores concise alternatives, the choice, rationale, sources, authority, consequences, and review trigger. It preserves conclusions and enough grounds for reassessment rather than hidden reasoning. Changed or disproved grounds mark affected conclusions for review while preserving the old record as history. Repeated questions are compared by stable obligation and captured premises. @status:spec/plan

An executor finding begins as a candidate. After verification, knowledge needed by other developers is promoted into a permanent specification, test, document, or other accepted project source with an addressable anchor. A local plan, event log, or worker report does not become the sole store of accepted project law. Source and evidence links remain with the promoted fact. @status:spec/plan

Computable identity, traversal, deduplication, coverage, transition, readiness, revision, and rule-expression questions are answered by bounded deterministic operations. Semantic relationship discovery, value, feasibility, architecture, and evidence sufficiency remain attributed judgments with sources and review triggers. Neither side claims the other's certainty. @status:spec/plan
5. Recursive lowering

The cycle is recursive: intent and expected outcome lead to unknown questions, facts, decisions, a work graph, valuable action, and a new observation. The same form applies to a campaign, workstream, or inner task. Active obligations, constraints, inputs, and acceptance flow downward; artifacts, evidence, and grounds for review flow upward. Canon: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-ADAPTIVE-CYCLE#root. This revises direction within the mandate as well as refining an old list. @status:spec/plan

Lowering turns a large outcome into executable tasks or internal stages. Input contains final acceptance, material invariants, available sources, dependencies, change scope, and delegated decisions. Output names concrete inputs, write and integration owners, expected behavior, selected checks, evidence, and safe boundary. A future command or test is marked as needing creation; detailed wording does not make it exist. @status:spec/plan

Lowering preserves obligations of the active outcome revision: every item receives implementation and verification, every deferral a closure location, and every new work item provenance. Outcome revision is separate: an old item may be retained, replaced, excluded under an authorized tradeoff, or found unattainable under named conditions; its history and unmet portion remain visible. Refining subwork does not cancel an obligation. Parent acceptance verifies integration and current parent criteria. Link and coverage checks are algorithmic; evidence meaning and sufficiency are assessed separately. @status:spec/plan

Recursion stops at a comprehensible action with a cheap sufficient check. Direct execution is allowed without extra planning. Distant work stays coarse with known obligations and a refinement trigger. Repeated lowering must resolve named uncertainty or a defect in the prior decomposition. Route corrections preserve earlier decisions and change reasons. @status:spec/plan

Semantic lowering, capability-specific rendering, strategic forks, stage-debt conservation, weak execution bundles, and Dreamer branches follow spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root. The specialized contract refines this recursive loop without replacing its obligation and acceptance semantics. @status:spec/plan
6. Prototype, functionality, and productization

Each outcome uses a sufficient route: direct execution; prototype followed by a finished solution; functional MVP followed by productization; or all three stages. Stages may remain inside one task. The 212 tasks are not automatically expanded into 636 stages. The route is justified by uncertainty, complexity, and verification cost. @status:spec/plan

A prototype completes a testable experiment and produces a conclusion, including a valuable disproof. A functional result implements the entire stated task scenario with material negative and recovery cases while keeping limitations visible. A productized result closes the full final contract and mandatory deferrals. An experiment may be accepted as an experiment; a consumer receives only established guarantees. An MVP bug does not become a requirement because a test records it. @status:spec/plan

The charter and packet may preauthorize suitable temporary deferral categories, including card and traceability work, final file organization, some architectural shells, doctests, and similar formal work. Actual scope is refined from the stage result. A deferral names its scope, reason, current-stage guarantees, owner, and evidence-backed closure obligation. A prototype need not first undergo full productization to receive this permission. @status:spec/plan

Deferral depends on requirement meaning and actual result use. If a standard shell protects an essential invariant, the temporary implementation protects it another way. Authority, truthful results, and preservation of actually affected data apply immediately. Isolated format research need not provide every public-migration guarantee; use by real consumers requires guarantees matching that use. @status:spec/plan

A prototype or MVP may remain in a separate worktree, branch, or marked experimental area with controlled connection. A commit records an artifact; it does not prove product readiness. Missing formal checks remain explicit, and widening a shared ratchet baseline or disabling a global gate does not close a deferral. Final acceptance discharges every required obligation; early use separately conforms to the charter and impact scope. @status:spec/plan

When it is unknown whether the architecture can satisfy final constraints, one representative slice is brought to those constraints early. It tests a specific risk such as a type boundary, serialization, or recovery. This is not an extra mandatory stage for every task. Rewriting a prototype preserves verified observations, independent behavior examples, and reasons for abandoning approaches. @status:spec/plan

Productizing one capability does not declare all of VibeVM beyond its overall prototype state. Product status, release version, artifact maturity, and work completion are independent. Changing the overall state remains a separate Owner decision. @status:spec/plan
7. Executors, verification, and recovery

An executor receives a bounded packet with exact sources, task, allowed route, read and write scope, resources, checks, and stop boundary. It refines subwork within that route without asking the Owner at every step. New authority, changed final acceptance, or crossing the boundary becomes a concrete coordinator proposal. The coordinator resolves ordinary delegated technical refinements; a worker does not accept its own result. @status:spec/plan

Independent ready tasks, bounded parts of one task, preparation, and verification of stable candidates may run in parallel. Actual read and write subjects, shared interfaces, resources, and one integration owner are bound before launch. Different filenames do not prove independence. The work window is limited by capacity to accept and integrate results; heavy commands are coordinated separately from executor count. @status:spec/plan

Select the affected build or test target and required cases first, including negative cases, invariants, and interface consumers. Valid evidence is reused only on the same material input. The full panel is not required per stage, worker, commit, or publication; it remains for an explicitly required final gate or justified cross-cutting impact. Mutation testing is used only for a concrete suspicion, with expected value and an attempt limit recorded. @status:spec/plan

The coordinator reads the actual result, compares it with the mandate and architecture, checks sufficient evidence, and only then changes acceptance. Independent review is selected for a material question and expected value rather than every line. A restart or new worker does not erase accepted history. A parent does not close merely because child rows are green when integration or obligations remain unverified. @status:spec/plan

After failure, quota loss, or account change, ZAP restores the charter, plan, evidence, current stage, debts, and live jobs. An unknown operation outcome is reconciled through receipt, job ID, or postconditions before repeating the effect. Lost reasoning is rebuilt from stored facts; hidden thoughts are not promised durable. Retries and diagnostics belong to the prior logical operation rather than a new session. @status:spec/plan

The coordinator distinguishes transient overload, no quota, an invalid request, and a product defect. It respects server hints and actual harness retries and does not stack independent infinite loops. Another account does not reset history or authorize moving secrets. Future continuation exists only through an actually configured authorized runtime; the specification does not promise an unstarted timer or background agent. @status:spec/plan

Changes preserve links among old and new behavior, affected users, migration, documentation, and verification. External documentation is connected only after defining source, revision, write owner, and build rules. A new revision rebinds only affected subjects and evidence. Temporary plans are removed after permanent requirements and unique knowledge move to project sources. @status:spec/plan

Closure compares original intent, the active authorized outcome revision, and actual benefit. It distinguishes original success, an achieved authorized approximation, partial result, and unattainability under current conditions. It requires truthful dispositions for original and current obligations, acceptance of required results, integration, closure of applicable deferrals, permanent knowledge placement, and a current final gate. An abandoned artifact need not be productized for an obsolete list; its real effects and the inapplicability of old formalities are checked. Empty frontier or exhausted quota is not success, and deleting hard items does not fulfill obligations. @status:spec/plan

One shared completion predicate governs scheduler, service, CLI, and backend closure. Active obligations, integration, applicable stage debt and deferrals, required evidence, pending selected economic changes or Owner decisions, change and campaign holds, incomplete admitted effects, unknown external outcomes, and required permanent knowledge block completion. Dormant alternatives and hypothetical Dreamer branches do not block unrelated closure. @status:spec/plan

ZAP durable milestones and selective planning
1. Observable outcomes

A canonical milestone has a stable typed identity independent of Work identity, display name and current decomposition. It names an observable result, its consumer or consequential decision, exact strategic/outcome scope and required obligations. Work can contribute to several milestones without duplicate execution or accounting. Existing group/phase/gate projections remain distinguishable from canonical milestones. No new game terrain or graphical client is required. @status:spec/plan

Milestone achievement is an explicit witnessed claim about required outcomes, never a count of completed children. Admission validates all required obligations and current applicable accepted evidence under existing central acceptance, outcome and source rules. An unproved obligation, rejected or stale evidence, foreign outcome, unsupported claim or missing applicability prevents achievement. A milestone receipt grants no campaign closure, charter authority, execution permission or resource release. @status:spec/plan

Achievement receipts retain immutable historical identity, source binding and evidence. Current validity is evaluated separately against relevant source and proof changes; relevant drift requires revalidation without erasing historical achievement. Unrelated commits do not invalidate the claim. Retirement and supersession preserve lineage, obligations, consumers, evidence and running-work identities. @status:spec/plan
2. Planning and materialization

Semantic proposal producers identify candidate milestones around observable consumer outcomes, decisions or independently provable capabilities. The kernel validates exact scope, required obligation coverage, dependencies, uniqueness and candidate rationale. It does not invent domain meaning from task titles. Discovery and inspection do not create executable work. Adopted planning state is distinguishable from a proposal and remains revisioned and inspectable. @status:spec/plan

Planning exposes relevant unsatisfied milestone boundaries, prerequisite blockers, uncovered obligations and the next justified refinement or information need. Only selected consequential work is materialized; distant work remains an explicit bounded horizon or unresolved debt. Required obligations cannot disappear because a frontier or query limit is reached. Shared work is counted once. Bounds are explicit, deterministic and fail or continue truthfully. @status:spec/plan

For an adopted milestone plan, the actual lowering/materialization path requires every new work item to identify the obligation/result it advances, blocker it resolves or selected information need, expected evidence/artifact and decision relevance. It checks retained work and evidence, explicit reuse/duplication dispositions and retry lineage. Unchosen alternatives and unselected optional information needs cannot manufacture runnable work. Title similarity is not semantic equivalence. The policy is enforced in the product path, not only in agent instructions. @status:spec/plan

Adopting or semantically revising milestone planning commitments uses the existing authority, economics, exact relevant basis, affected-scope, holds and safe-stop boundaries. Initial milestone creation and first plan adoption may use a validated initial-baseline classification only for an exact candidate strategy and active charter/intent/outcome before any adopted milestone plan or lowering, with no imported active/accepted/unresolved work mistaken for a fresh baseline. Later dynamic additions remain semantic changes even before external execution starts. New data-proposal records cannot bypass privileged admission by calling themselves annotations. Existing campaigns without an adopted milestone plan retain established behavior. New planning state must not silently opt itself out on relowering, route changes or strategy revision. @status:spec/plan
3. Information decisions

An information opportunity names the material decision, alternatives or unknown condition, observation sought, applicability sources, acquisition and verification cost, delay where known, expected decision improvement or explicit uncertainty, and a stopping rule. It references existing sources, questions, regions, forks or horizons where applicable. It is reusable information potential, not execution capacity, and its existence alone creates no task or completion blocker. @status:spec/plan

A deterministic bounded selection query compares declared decision benefit with acquisition, verification, delay and coordination costs using compatible units and explicit ranges or unknown judgments. It identifies dominated opportunities and cheaper decisive observations without manufacturing probabilities or precise scores. Unknown or overlapping estimates remain inspectable rather than silently becoming zero. Selection names its rationale and relevant source binding; materialization still uses ordinary admitted research/probe work. @status:spec/plan

Selected information work retains a stable opportunity-to-Work binding and uses existing work types, contracts, cost and resource accounting. Retries cannot create unrelated duplicate tasks. Retained applicable evidence and prior acquisitions remain reusable. Relevant decision/source drift forces reconsideration; optional unresolved opportunities never become mandatory acceptance requirements. A useful observation may expose more uncertainty. @status:spec/plan
4. Explicit graph changes

Typed split, merge, contribution move, route change and retirement proposals carry operation identity, exact before-state binding, stable predecessor/successor mapping and reason. A read-only dry run exposes changed identities, memberships, edges, proof applicability and conservation results before application. Applying uses the same validation and normal semantic admission. Retries reconcile the same operation; old journal entries and historical receipts are never rewritten. @status:spec/plan

Transformations preserve every surviving obligation, consumer, shared contribution and dependency or explicitly account for its authorized disposition. Splits conserve the union of obligations and work; merges deduplicate by identity and explicitly reconcile acceptance boundaries. Retired or dormant alternatives remain traceable. Cycles, dangling references, silent obligation loss, unsupported proof carryover and conflicting mappings refuse. Presentation-only changes are distinct from semantic changes. @status:spec/plan

A milestone change preserves original task, contract, packet, attempt and external-effect identities. A proposal affecting execution must pass existing affected-job and safe-stop handling before application; it cannot release unknown-effect reservations or manufacture completion. Pure membership movement that leaves execution scope unchanged must say so and still preserve evidence applicability. @status:spec/plan
5. Public behavior and verification

Registered domain commands and bounded queries make canonical milestones, historical/current achievement, opportunities, focus and transformation previews available through the existing machine, authenticated HTTP and CLI surfaces. Object cards use names, result/consumer descriptions, meaningful typed relationships, explicit missing data and underlying stable IDs. Existing independent effort, elapsed time, complexity, difficulty and uncertainty assessments remain available without becoming dispatch authority. @status:spec/plan

Acceptance requires persisted command/query and real lowering-path tests for coverage, proof freshness, selective refinement, information selection/reuse, every supported transformation, stale/retry/reopen behavior, no authority bypass and no historical loss. Source traceability, formatting, strict lint, conformance, public use and clean offline package installation/build remain required. The Owner explicitly excludes a comparative agent pilot from this goal; no empirical productivity improvement is claimed. @status:spec/plan

A simulated transcript may demonstrate wire mechanics only and is labeled simulated. A weak local execution mode remains a normative capability without a claim that current Qwen quality has been tested. @status:spec/plan

Clients receive machine-readable capabilities, revision-bound bounded queries, explanations, snapshots, commands, and event tails keyed by StoreId, BaseId, Revision, and cursor. 6. Migration and release acceptance

Migration captures the complete shared or user-local MUP plan, every task contract and legacy constraint, original bytes and hash domains, and an exact identity, obligation, evidence, and authority-classification map into a separate recoverable Rust store. It validates before switching the store pointer and never starts NEXT. Temporary campaign specifications and prototype material may be retired only after unique requirements, decisions, behavior mappings, provenance, and accepted evidence are promoted to permanent project sources. ZAP: Rust runtime, transactional storage, and bounded queries
1. Production language and module boundaries

All ZAP-owned production executable source is Rust, including the domain kernel, transactional application service, storage and index engine, scheduler, protocol validation, CLI, machine backend, and executable adapter helpers. XML, Markdown, JSON, TOML, and English prompts remain data. Python may remain isolated as historical prototype or investigation material, but ordinary build, installation, execution, migration, and verification of the Rust product do not invoke it. @status:spec/plan

The package-owned Cargo workspace separates pure domain transitions, transactional application admission, storage and bounded queries, runtime and effects, host and project adapters, and thin entrypoints. SemanticProvider and AgentHost are distinct. Pure reducers call no clock, network, filesystem, model, worker, or external command. Effects enter through prepared intents and captured observations. @status:spec/plan

The package declares every code-bearing dependency and installs from its shipped source without a path into the VibeVM source checkout, an undeclared global tool, a committed binary blob, or a Python facade. Stable project capabilities are consumed through published protocols or adapters. An implementation convenience in the host repository is not a distribution contract. @status:spec/plan
2. Canonical events and atomic state

A StoreId and BaseId bind immutable imported material to an ordered logical event history. Revision, EventId, CommandId, causal predecessors, and reducer or semantic epoch are explicit. An event sequence is semantic authority; exported XML or JSON, materialized indexes, snapshots, GOAL.md, viewer state, and caches are derived and cannot grant authority or replace missing history. @status:spec/plan

One supported mutation atomically commits one LogicalEvent, its CAS and idempotency receipt, one Sequence and Revision advancement, and every mandatory projection or index mutation needed for safe subsequent admission. A failure commits none of that transition or leaves an explicitly recoverable prepared intent. The storage ADR selects one durability model; independently written files and tables are not described as one atomic operation. @status:spec/plan

Canonical JSON is limited to validated ingress and immutable event bytes. Domain reducers receive typed payloads and return typed projection mutations; they do not repeatedly parse arbitrary JSON or infer event meaning from strings. Wire validation, canonical byte identity, semantic transition, and storage commit remain explicit seams. @status:spec/plan

Exactly one current controller epoch may admit mutations for a campaign. Recovered, duplicated, or stale controllers cannot reuse old admission authority. Idempotency binds one CommandId to one exact payload and result. External effects remain separately reconciled because database atomicity cannot promise exactly-once behavior from an arbitrary host. @status:spec/plan

Content-addressed large artifacts may live outside transactional rows only through a recoverable publication protocol that binds content identity, committed references, temporary state, final location, and cleanup or repair. A committed reference never silently points to an unpublished object, and an orphan does not become accepted evidence. @status:spec/plan
3. Mandatory indexes and bounded navigation

The committed store indexes stable entity identities, hierarchy, typed edges in both directions, source-to-dependent relations, obligation coverage, readiness and blockers, evidence applicability, open encounters, packets and attempts, active claims and effects, holds, and completion blockers. Indexes bind schema, semantic and query versions and committed cursor and are rebuilt or invalidated rather than trusted under an incompatible identity. @status:spec/plan

Known affected views update from changed subjects and reverse dependencies. The runtime does not replay all history, duplicate the whole plan per DreamBranch, scan the complete store for each ordinary command, or eagerly materialize every transitive closure without measurement. Missing semantic edges remain an explicit closure uncertainty that algorithms cannot erase. @status:spec/plan

The service supplies revision-bound and paginated node lookup, search, ancestors, dependents, frontier, readiness explanation, affected subgraph, revision comparison, fork reading, packet generation, source detail, why, and attempt resume. Every bounded response states scope, completeness, omitted or unloaded regions, and a continuation cursor. An unvisited region is never returned as an empty or risk-free graph. @status:spec/plan

Snapshots and event tails bind StoreId, BaseId, schema and semantic epoch, reducer and query identity, Revision, last included EventId, and cursor. Duplicate delivery is idempotent; gaps, foreign bases, stale pages, partial final writes, and unsupported versions are explicit. Replay and snapshot-plus-tail projections are required to agree at the same committed boundary. @status:spec/plan

Graph traversal, deduplication, ordering, reference validation, coverage, blocker counting, source lookup, diffing, and cursor continuation must be bounded Rust operations usable by weak and strong agents and future clients. They do not require loading the complete graph into a model or invoking a model to open a view. @status:spec/plan
4. Recovery, checkpoints, and cold trust

Durable state retains charter and outcome revisions, strategic and Lowering lineage, active fork grounds, task contracts, stages and debt, source captures, proof applicability, packets, attempts, claims, DispatchIntents, ExternalJobHandles and receipts, pending effects, holds, safe boundaries, and the next admissible action. A bounded resume projection reconstructs this state after compaction, crash, process or account replacement; it is checked against actual workspace and host observations before action. @status:spec/plan

Write-ahead intent precedes an external effect. A crash or missing receipt leaves an explicit unknown outcome. Recovery reconciles the bound external identity or postconditions before reissue, preserves attempts and failure classification, and never interprets context loss as permission to reset an approach counter or repeat an effect. @status:spec/plan

Normal fast reopen may trust crash-safe transactions and a version-bound durable checkpoint only under a documented trusted-local-store boundary in which workers cannot write the store or checkpoint and supported mutation uses the Rust service. Legacy import, explicit distrustful audit, identity mismatch, or deployment without that confinement rederives and validates from canonical history or uses an independent trust anchor. A version label, timestamp, self-hash, or worker promise alone does not establish integrity, and no claim covers a hostile operating-system administrator. @status:spec/plan

Recovery locates the last complete confirmed boundary, preserves corrupt bytes and command ambiguity, and records authorized repair. Middle corruption is not skipped and a partial tail is not treated as completed. While an associated external result is unknown, repair does not authorize repeating it. @status:spec/plan
5. Epochs, legacy import, and portability

The Rust store, wire, codec, reducer, and query contracts use explicit version or epoch identities. New stores use StoreEpoch zap/2; read-only legacy import uses LegacyEpoch::Zap1 with domain-separated legacy digests and an explicit identity map. Zap/1 bytes and hashes are not silently reinterpreted under Rust serialization, and package release version remains independently governed. @status:spec/plan

Migration preserves original bytes, identities, order, hierarchy, dependencies, contracts, obligations, evidence, authority classifications, unknown extensions, and legacy digest domains. Codec mapping addresses ordering, escaping, numbers and non-finite values, reserved tags, duplicate members, Unicode, newlines, date and time values, and machine-local paths. Imported state is validated before changing the configured store pointer, and recovery material remains available. @status:spec/plan

Importing, inspecting, upgrading, installing, or publishing ZAP does not activate the unrelated NEXT campaign. The 425-node and 212-task data set is migration and query evidence only. Current unaccepted prototype candidates retain candidate provenance and cannot become accepted Rust behavior through porting. @status:spec/plan

ZAP operates in an ordinary VibeVM project through discovered or bound project identity, source handles, package capabilities, user-local context, workspace adapter, toolchain, and verification commands. VibeVM repository paths, Windows paths, pilot IDs, GitHub accounts, and project-specific commands remain fixtures or configuration. Offline, rootless-home, container, and non-GitHub use do not require a central service. @status:spec/plan
6. Truthful operation and performance

Versioned machine views expose strategy and execution links, lowering and packet provenance, stages and debt, knowledge and fog, sources, evidence applicability, forks and DreamBranches, costs, role routing, packet composition and omissions, dispatch receipts, liveness, retries, decisions, holds, stop state, completion blockers, invalidation, and repair. Credentials and private sensitive transport data remain excluded. Opening a view performs no semantic reassessment. @status:spec/plan

Handler, schema, command, query, transport, and adapter registries publish only actually available operations and versions. Unsupported commands and unknown variants are refused. A planned field, fixture, simulated weak transcript, or prototype behavior is not reported as implemented capability. @status:spec/plan

Rust does not by itself prove scale or latency. Declared node, edge, event-history, hardware, cold and warm state, write durability, memory, storage growth, and invalidation fanout accompany performance evidence. Small bounded queries target interactive behavior; long import, audit, rebuild, or large-fanout operations report progress, incomplete results, and resumable boundaries. Proposed numerical targets remain hypotheses until measured. @status:spec/plan
7. Permanent references

Canonical entity and evidence meaning comes from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root. Authority, closure, runtime effects, and public admission come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root and spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUNTIME#root. Agent and packet records come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root. @status:spec/plan

An execution resource referenced by a contract does not acquire known capacity, availability or a richer description merely by being referenced. Optional opportunities do not become runnable or completion-blocking merely by appearing on a map. @status:spec/plan
3. Optional descriptive data

A separate revisioned map-work assessment record may add a display label/explanation, remaining effort/time ranges, structural complexity, executor-relative difficulty, uncertainty and evidence to an existing materialized WorkId. Its data-proposal command is descriptive only: it changes no Work, contract, charter, approval, completion, resource allocation or dispatch state. Exact record CAS and command retry remain enforced. The initial assessment scope is existing Work records, including container/gate work; other object kinds expose existing information or explicit unassessed/reference-only state. No generic semantic conclusion is parsed into a numeric grade. @status:spec/plan

Assessment ingress checks a reproducible current source fingerprint of the Work and its applicable active contract data. A stale supplied source basis refuses. The assessment's own record and unrelated store commits are excluded from that fingerprint. Reads classify recorded metadata as current, stale or unavailable against the same algorithm. Stale descriptive data remains inspectable with provenance but cannot silently become a current estimate or authoritative task text. Active-contract selection reuses the existing complete indexed policy; no arbitrary first contract is chosen. @status:spec/plan

Remaining agent effort, elapsed duration, passive wait, structural complexity, difficulty and uncertainty are separate fields. Complexity and difficulty use independently explained low/medium/high grades with unassessed distinct from low. Assessed difficulty states executor/knowledge assumptions. Unknowns and confidence/precision are explicit; no invented probability or consequence-as-difficulty mapping is permitted. Ranges validate their bounds after deserialization; unknown upper bounds remain unknown. Assessment evidence is declared descriptive evidence and does not become acceptance or observed host capability. @status:spec/plan

Existing economics forecasts retain their change/assessment scope, baseline, team assumptions, evidence and relevant basis. They are not automatically mapped to arbitrary Work or routes. A supplied work estimate states its source and assumptions; no cost-prose parsing occurs. Current typed descriptive assessments may inform human views, while algorithmic routing and admission remain governed by their existing validated inputs. @status:spec/plan
4. Route interpretation

A route view validates an explicit selection of distinct source-plan WorkIds and their relevant prerequisite closure under a finite budget. It preserves edge kinds, checks cycles/dangling dependencies and reports omitted prerequisites and unresolved blockers. Repeated IDs never multiply cost. Agent effort aggregates only comparable current estimates and counts shared work once. Known subtotals are distinct from a complete estimate; missing or stale estimates cannot become zero. Elapsed results are supplied estimates or explicitly labeled precedence-only lower bounds under stated assumptions, never a claim to a resource-feasible schedule or a naive sum of parallel durations. A route or map distance does not authorize execution. @status:spec/plan

The data model contains semantic object/relation kinds and inspectable measures, not terrain, icons, colors or pixel distances. A later client may map those meanings to towns, roads, forests or fog. Geometry cannot replace authoritative units/ranges. Display-only enrichment is optional and cannot block algorithm work. @status:spec/plan
5. Public integration and preservation

Registered typed domain queries expose overview, exact cards and route/relationship meaning through the existing machine Query request, authenticated HTTP query path and CLI read entrypoint. Query IDs appear through the actual registry. A new generic transport, runtime frontier replacement or model invocation is not required. Public types have real usage documentation and meaningful source/store/transport evidence. @status:spec/plan

A read-only projection of the completed development campaign preserves all21identities,49planning dependencies and9distinct acceptance dependencies. Its six outcome groups are a presentation candidate; they create no whole-group execution barriers. It is not a canonical Work store or an authorization to import, migrate or execute NEXT. Independent actual-service fixtures verify the product query and assessment paths. @status:spec/plan

Version1.1 development preserves released1.0 source and tag. Existing records, commands, queries, logical history and runtime admission keep their current semantics. New descriptive records and queries are explicitly registered; no historical byte rewriting, baseline widening, gate exemption or silent schema substitution is allowed. The first implementation has no new canonical milestone acceptance authority, graphical client or live campaign migration. @status:spec/plan
